analysis: Examined docs/provider/cli-reference.md base lines 1726-1974 and head lines 1-396. The changes are documentation-only: the date bump at head line 3, a new `addon` subcommand row at head line 156, and a new `darkbloom addon` section at head lines 904-932 (only partially visible in the patch excerpt). The section describes operator debugging of add-on holds through the owner-only lifecycle mailbox, bound to the live process identity, with add-ons using a separate local socket (docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md). The change at head line 1758 is not visible in the supplied units. The base-side file/env tables (e.g. lines 1730-1743, 1855-1931) were reviewed for context and show no security-relevant change. This documentation reveals a new local attack surface: an add-on hold IPC (socket plus mailbox commands) in which other local processes can influence provider residency or availability. That surface is relevant to TB-003 (operator vs process) and resembles the fan-helper IPC pattern (TB-010/T-044). The threat model has no entry for add-on holds. No implementation source (AddonCommand.swift, addon-hold IPC) was supplied, so authentication of the socket, hold bounds/expiry and the effect on the drain/serving and authorization state (T-053) are unverified. No concrete regression is citable from docs alone. Integration should check the implementation for socket ownership/peer validation, hold lease bounds, and whether holds can block drain, logout or revocation, and should consider whether the threat model needs a new add-on hold boundary entry.
